description:
FILED s464 (Fable, 2026-09-02) from an sb-sprof profile of the fib(27) row on main 3d666ea: THROW 2.5 % + p-return-value 4.6 % of samples, and a direct A/B -- `sub fib { my $n = shift; return $n < 2 ? $n : fib($n-1)+fib($n-2) }` vs the same sub with the bare tail expression -- 3x fib(27) wall (startup included, best of 3): 0.420 s vs 0.396 s, 0.425 vs 0.398, 0.499 vs 0.411 -- ~25 ms of ~250 ms compute, ~10 %.  THE EMISSION: `(p-sub pl-fib (&rest %_args) (p-raw-params ($n) (p-return (p-?: ...))))` -- a `return` as the LAST statement of a sub body still lowers to (p-return X) = (throw :p-return (let ((*wantarray* *pcl-caller-wantarray*)) (p-return-value X))), caught by the frame catch one level up.  perl: a return in tail position IS the sub value; the only observable parts are the caller-context restore (the tail statement already gets p-caller-ctx) and p-return-value normalisation (scalar-context array -> count; multi-value list build) which the tail-list shape `(if *wantarray* (vector ...) (progn ...))` and the #964 frame exit (%p-leavesub) already provide.  DESIGN: in Parser2 _lower_body_regime, a last statement `return EXPR` (no modifier) lowers as the tail expression EXPR would; `return (LIST)` as the tail list; bare `return;` as `(if (eq *wantarray* t) (%p-empty-list) nil)`.  A conditional trailing return (`return X if C;`) and a return nested in a compound tail (`if (c) { return 1 } else { return 2 }`) are the second step, only if measured worth it.  Register as a Kind-A emission (`tail-return`) so PCL_OPT=none runs the general form identically.  BAR: corpus-diff every diff explained (the shape is everywhere); emission-ab; the full sweep (every tail return moves); companion op/sub.t + op/ --quick; bench all rows main vs branch with a control pair; guards: value/context probes for scalar/list/void callers of a tail-returning sub incl. `return @a` in scalar ctx, `return ($x, $y)`, `return wantarray ? ... : ...`, `return;`, `return undef`, and a sub whose tail return is inside eval { }.  Owner: the perf slot after AX (#985/#982).

== DONE (s465bb, Opus round 23, 2026-09-03; worktree agent-a58611fd5d94e5849) ==

SHIPPED.  A `return EXPR` that IS a sub body's LAST statement (no statement
modifier, single expression) lowers as the tail expression.  Emission:
  (p-tail-value X)                 single-statement body
  (p-caller-ctx (p-tail-value X))  multi-statement body (:void regime)
  (p-return-empty)                 bare `return;` in tail position
Files: Pl/Parser2.pm (_lower_body_regime records the body's last live statement
by refaddr in $self->{_body_tail_stmt}, localised; the existing Break branch
owns eligibility after its modifier + comma gates), Pl/Passes.pm (Kind-A name
`tail-return`), cl/pcl-runtime.lisp (`p-tail-value`, `p-return-empty`, both
exported; p-return's zero-arg branch now spells its answer with the same
macro), docs/ir-spec.md Â§5.3, Pl/t/tail-return-01.t.
Generation v2-590 -> v2-610; the three checked-in artifacts regenerated.

THE DESIGN CORRECTION THE TASK DID NOT ANTICIPATE, and it is the load-bearing
finding.  The task's sketch said the tail form needs no normalisation because
"%p-leavesub already provides it".  MEASURED FALSE: two of p-return-value's
arms fire on a value the frame exit does NOT repeat -- an ARRAY (adjustable
vector) in SCALAR context is its element COUNT, and raw nil in LIST context is
the empty list.  With the plain elision,
  my @arr=(7,8,9); sub f { my $z=0; return @arr } print f() . "";
printed ARRAY(0x1) where perl prints 3 (probe scratch/arrctx.pl: four sub
spellings x twelve consumers, run under perl and ./runpcl side by side).
`p-tail-value` is therefore p-return-value with its IDENTITY fast path
inlined: p-return-value is the identity on every value that is neither raw NIL
nor a raw NON-STRING VECTOR -- a claim read off its own arms, since every BOX
arm is applied again by %p-leavesub at the frame exit.  Two type tests, no
call, and the rare shapes reach the ONE existing rule, so there is no second
copy of the normalisation.

WHAT WAS REJECTED, and why it must not be retried: moving the array->count
rule into %p-leavesub (which would also have fixed the pre-existing implicit-
tail divergence).  %p-leavesub reads *wantarray*, and the `insensitive-call`
Kind-A gate deliberately omits the context bind at call sites whose callee's
returns are provably scalar-rooted -- a VALUE rule keyed on *wantarray* there
would be right only by accident.  (It would also miss `@a . ""` with no sub at
all, which is the real bug: #1039.)

BARS, with numbers.
- corpus-diff vs 1fed80b: 31 of 111 files differ, silent drops 5 unchanged.
  emission-ab --ref over lib/**/*.pm: 18 of 22 DIFF, RCDIFF 0.
- EVERY ONE of those diffs is attributable to the gate, PROVED rather than
  argued: re-transpiling the populations with PCL_OPT=-tail-return and byte-
  comparing against a 1fed80b worktree gives perl-tests SAME 111 / DIFF 0,
  lib SAME 22 / DIFF 0, SHAPES SAME 6 / DIFF 0 (scratch/ab-off.pl).  So the
  general form is untouched and the whole diff is the three shape classes plus
  re-indentation and the gen stamp.
- Full sweep (--jobs 8): GATE clean, TOTAL passing 18266 (+0), drops 5 =
  census, 0 new / 0 fixed; the 4 UNSTABLE + 15 unverified rows are the usual
  PARTIAL-file noise the tool itself labels.
- Gate: 194 files / 6567 rows, only the 13 pclxs xs rows failing (they are
  ignored per the USER).  Exactly TWO gate rows moved, both stale guards of
  the replaced shape, repaired in the same commit (the s416 rule):
  parser2-01.t's bare-return row (now asserts BOTH positions -- a
  strengthening) and decl-ordering-01.t's relative-order row.
- Probes: scratch/probes.pl (91 rows: context, the copy rule, local, eval
  frames, sort comparators, goto &sub, anon subs, @_ shapes, blessed identity,
  dualvar $!) byte-identical to perl 5.40.3 on the DEFAULT path, under
  PCL_OPT=none and under PCL_OPT=-tail-return.
- Compile time (interleaved best-of-3): pack.t 4.07 s -> 3.93 s, sprintf.t
  0.48 -> 0.47.  No cost.
- BENCH (scratch/wallab.pl, interleaved wall-time A/B of two saved cores, K=5,
  load average 3; CONTROL = the same tree against itself, 0.983x-1.062x, so
  +-6.2 % is the floor).  main 605b837 -> branch, absolute exec seconds:
    fibret   0.6979 -> 0.4782  0.685x   (-31.5 %)
    gcdret   0.1103 -> 0.0978  0.887x   (-11.3 %)
    subret   0.1141 -> 0.1025  0.898x   (-10.2 %)
    methret  0.3379 -> 0.3101  0.918x   (-8.2 %)
    fib(27)x 0.4692 -> 0.4633  0.987x   implicit tail: the gate cannot touch it
    gcdrec   0.1099 -> 0.1085  0.987x   modifier returns: likewise
    slices   0.1873 -> 0.1863  0.995x   ovlsub 1.004x   symref 0.993x
    arrhash  0.0869 -> 0.0939  1.080x = NOISE (1.011x on a K=7 re-run; the
             CONTROL read 1.062x on this very row; its loop has no sub call)
  A FINDING FOR THE NEXT PERF SESSION: the STANDING bench rows are BLIND to
  this transform -- bench-exec's fib body ends in an implicit tail and
  gcdrec's returns carry modifiers -- which is why the three new rows were
  needed.  The cleanest statement of the win: on main a fib written with an
  explicit tail `return` cost 0.698 s against the implicit tail's 0.469 s,
  49 % more for the same program; on the branch the two spellings are 0.478
  and 0.463, i.e. the same sub.

WHAT IS NOT DONE (deliberately, and named):
- A multi-element `return (A, B)` still throws: Parser2 gates a top-level
  comma to the v1 seam BEFORE the tail branch, so the task's "return (LIST) as
  the tail list" would have meant touching the v1 text emitter.  Left.
- A `return` under a statement modifier, one nested in a compound/loop
  (`if (c) { return 1 } else { return 2 }`), and one inside eval {} or a sort
  comparator all still throw.  The task named the compound-tail case as step 2
  "only if measured worth it"; it was NOT measured here.
- The pre-existing implicit-tail divergence is FILED, not fixed: #1039.

GUARD: Pl/t/tail-return-01.t, 9 rows -- four VALUE programs (two of them re-run
under PCL_OPT=none) covering scalar/list/void context, the wantarray-conditional
return, the array count, the bare/undef/empty edges, an earlier return plus a
tail return, the #964 copy at every aliasing consumer, `local` restored at the
frame exit after the value is taken, the frames that are NOT sub frames (eval,
sort comparator, goto &sub), object identity -- and five SHAPE rows.
INVERSE-VERIFIED on a 1fed80b worktree: exactly the 3 tail-shape rows fail
there and every value row passes (they are semantic invariants).
subject: Perf: a TAIL-position `return EXPR` is a THROW through the frame catch plus p-return-value -- eliding it to the bare tail expression is ~10 % on fib(27) (measured s464), and every return-ending sub pays it
